A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the banking law, in relation to conforming the regulation of mortgage loan originators in New York Law to the federal law; and to repeal article 12-E of such law relating thereto
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A6924A

TITLE  OF  BILL:    An  act  to  amend the banking law, in relation to
conforming the regulation of mortgage loan originators in New York Law
to the federal law; and to repeal article 12-E of  such  law  relating
thereto

Purpose  Or  General  Idea  Of  Bill:    This  bill  would conform the
regulation of mortgage loan originators ("MLOs") in New York State  to
the requirements under federal law.

Summary Of Specific Provisions:  Section 1 of the bill repeals Article
12-E  of the Banking Law and adds a new Article 12-E that conforms the
regulation of MLOs in New York to Title V of Public Law  110-289,  the
Housing  and  Economic  Recovery  Act  of 2008. Specifically, Title V,
known as the "Secure and Fair Enforcement for Mortgage  Licensing  Act
of  2008"  ("SAFE  Act"), is intended to implement a uniform system of
MLO licensing  at  the  State  level.  The  SAFE  Act  authorizes  the
Department  of  Housing  and  Urban  Development ("HUD") to assume the
licensing of MLOs in  any  state  that  does  not  enact  implementing
legislation  acceptable  to  HUD by August 1, 2009. While the SAFE Act
licensing system does not differ dramatically from the current  system
for  authorizing  MLOs  in  New  York,  it  will introduce several new
concepts, including the concept that applicants  for  an  MLO  license
will  have  to  pass  a  written  test,  maintain a financial bond and
satisfy ongoing, national  educational  standards  to  maintain  their
licensed status.

In   addition,   applicants   with  a  felony  conviction  for  fraud,
dishonesty" breach of trust, or money laundering (or any other  felony
within  seven  years  of  the  date of application) cannot be licensed
under the SAFE Act or this bill The SAFE  Act  also  will  change  the
definitions applicable to MLOs.

A short summary of revised Article 12-E follows:

a.  Section  599-a  contains  the  legislative purpose, which is to be
consistent with the SAFE Act.

b. Section 599-b defines terms used in the  Article,  including  "Loss
processor  or  underwriter,"  "clerical  or support duties," "mortgage
loan originator," "residential mortgage loan" and "Nationwide Mortgage
Licensing System and Registry."

c. Section 599-c requires individuals who engage in the business of  a
mortgage   loan   originator   with   respect  to  any  "dwelling"  or
"residential  real  property"  to  be  licensed  as  a  mortgage  loan
originator  ("MLO"),  and  contains  a transition rule for individuals
licensed under the existing version of Article 12- E. It also contains
exemptions from registration for certain persons,  including  licensed
attorneys  who  negotiate mortgage loans as an ancillary matter to the
attorney's representation of the client (unless they  are  compensated
by the lender). Finally, this section requires independent contractors
who  are  loan  processors  or  underwriters  to be licensed under the
article.  (Current  article  12-E  exempts  them,  but  the  SAFE  Act
specifically covers them.)


d.  Section  599-d  lays out the process for registering to be an MLO,
including application forms  and  what  must  be  disclosed  on  them,
charges  to  mortgage  banker  and  broker  firms to cover the cost of
registering MLOs that work for them, fee collection by the NMLSR,  and
electronic filing.

e.  Section  599-e  contains the findings the Superintendent must make
before issuing a license to be  an  MLO.  The  principal  change  from
current Article 12-E is that an applicant may not be granted a license
if  he or she has been convicted of, or pled guilty or nolo contendere
to, a felony in a domestic, foreign or military court: (i) during  the
past  7  years,  or  (ii)  at  any  time  preceding  the  date  of the
application, in the case of a felony involving fraud, dishonesty or  a
breach  of  trust, or money laundering. This section also requires the
written test and surety bond.

f Section 599-f requires prospective licensees to complete at least 23
hours of education courses that have been approved by the NMLSR.

g. Section 599-g requires applicants to pass  a  written  test  before
they are licensed.

h. Section 599-h requires mortgage bankers or brokers to submit to the
NMLSR reports of condition in such form as the NMLSR may require.

i. Section 599-i specifies that, in order for a license to be renewed,
the MLO must continue to meet the minimum standards for insurance of a
license, must satisfy the annual continuing education requirements and
must have paid the required renewal fees.

j.   Section   599-j   sets  forth  the  annual  continuing  education
requirements.

k. Section 599-k sets out the requirement for MLOs, or their employing
firms, to maintain a mortgage loan originator.

l. Section 599-1 requires the superintendent to report  on  a  regular
basis all violations of the Article.

m.  Section  599-m  requires  mortgage  bankers  and brokers to retain
documentation of the completion of education courses.

n. Section 599-n sets forth the authority  of  the  superintendent  to
revoke or suspend a license for certain violations of the law.

o.  Section  599-0  authorizes  the  superintendent  to make rules and
regulations for licensing.

p. Section 599-p. This section requires that  MLOs  put  their  unique
identifier  on  all  residential  mortgage  loan application forms and
other documents required by the superintendent.

q. Section 599-q. This section  provide  for  the  confidentiality  of
information provided to the superintendent.


r.  Section  599-r  provides  rules  of  construction that ensure that
nothing in Article 12E will be deemed to impair any of the  provisions
of article 12-D.

Sections  2  and  3  of the bill make certain technical changes to the
Banking Law.

Section 4 of the bill provides that the Superintendent may charge fees
for the licensing of MLOs and may use any reasonable methods necessary
to timely implement Article 12-E of the Banking Law.

Section 5 of the bill provides for the effective date of the bill.

Effects Of Present Law Which This Bill Would Alter:  Article 12-E  was
originally  added  to  the  Banking  Law by Chapter 744 of the Laws of
2006. It was substantially amended by Chapter 553 of the laws of 2007.
The current version of  Article  12-E,  which  was  effective  at  the
beginning  of  2008,  provides  for the "authorization" of individuals
seeking to act as MLOs in New York.

Justification:  This bill would demonstrate the commitment of New York
to maintain its regulation of MLOs. Indeed,  absent  this  regulation,
New  York  would  cede  this  important  responsibility to the federal
government. The  bill  also  would  make  New  York's  system  of  MLO
regulation  consistent  with  that used in other states, thus reducing
the cost of regulation for all entities, particularly those  operating
in  multiple  states.    The legislation also will serve as a model of
interstate cooperation, thus serving to enhance  the  dual  regulatory
system for financial services providers in the United States.

Prior Legislative History:  This is a new bill.

Fiscal  implications  For State And Local Governments:  This bill will
not have an impact on state finances.

Effective Date:   This act shall take  effect  immediately;  provided,
however,  that sections two and three of this act shall take effect on
the same date and the same manner as sections 15 and 16 of chapter 472
of the laws of 2008 take effect, respectively, and provided,  further,
that  the  superintendent of banks may delay the implementation of any
provision of this act if consistent with title V of  The  Housing  and
Economic Recovery Act of 2008, Pub. L. No. 110-287.
